subject: Music Production
title: Equal Loudness and Fletcher-Munson
description: A fast breakdown of Equal Loudness and Fletcher-Munson for builders.

hook.text: In the 1930s, Harvey Fletcher and Wilden Munson tested how people perceive loudness at different pitches.

buildup.text: They discovered that human ears are most sensitive to midrange frequencies around two to four kilohertz.

discovery.text: Bass and treble need to be physically louder than midrange to sound equally loud to our ears.

twist.text: This is why music sounds thin and weak at low volumes—the bass seems to disappear.

climax.text: Producers use these curves to mix at proper levels so every frequency sounds balanced.

punchline.text: Our ears cheat—they hear some frequencies better.

quiz.question: Why does music sound thin at low volumes?
options: Our ears are less sensitive to bass at lower levels
Bass notes take longer to reach our ears
